subject: Post-demo recap + snapshot & temporary model hold request
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@axionpay.com>, AxionPay Security <sec@axionpay.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo recap + snapshot & temporary model hold request

Hi Daniel / team — thanks again for taking the demo this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps based on what we heard: 

- Key fit notes: your batch document classification workload favors concise context windows (avg 512 tokens) and high precision on entity extraction. The models we recommend for initial pilot are: Redwood-Local-13B-quant (best latency/cost tradeoff), and Redwood-Chat-7B-q4f for edge-case generation filtering.
- Risks we flagged: after a recent runtime model rollout (v4.4), a small subset of prompts in your QA set returned different entity tokenization vs our previous stable variant (v4.3.2). This created higher false positive rates in our internal lab.

What I’m asking from you now:
1) Can you confirm whether you want Redwood to temporarily route AxionPay production traffic to the snapshoted variant (v4.3.2) while we validate the v4.4 diffs? This is a temporary "hold" (non-breaking, reversible) we can place within minutes — it preserves your current behavior.
2) Please review the attached evaluation prompts and the quick benchmark summary I’ve attached. If you can share a 2–4 person review window by Wednesday 11/4, we can complete the mutual action plan (MAP) below.

Attachments included: axion_benchmarks_summary.xlsx, eval_prompts_axion.txt
Links: evaluation artifacts & bench console -> https://redwood.example.com/evals/AXP-1147/results

Proposed MAP:
- Today (11/2): Redwood prepares a snapshot and diff report (we attach the initial summary).
- 11/3: AxionPay security / engineering validate on a small sample.
- 11/4: Decide on a release path for v4.4 or keep v4.3.2 pinned for pilot.

If you prefer, we can proactively pin to v4.3.2 now and unpin on your go-ahead. Pinning is reversible and we’ll provide a post-mortem of the diffs once our triage completes. Let me know which path you prefer.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-2819
--
Redwood Inference

From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@axionpay.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: AxionPay Security <sec@axionpay.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 09:25:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + snapshot & temporary model hold request

Marissa — appreciate the quick recap and the artifacts. A couple quick clarifying questions before we decide:

1) If you pin to v4.3.2 now, will there be any interruption to latency SLA? We need to be sure performance stays within our P50/P95 targets.
2) Can you show a targeted diff example where the entity tokenization changed? We can route a small internal dataset to validate.

From a security perspective, our team prefers to pause changes that affect production inference behavior until we’ve validated. If it’s low overhead for Redwood, we’d like you to do a temporary hold while our engineers run the sample checks (we’ll try to get that back to you by EOD 11/3).

Thanks —
Daniel Park
Head of ML Platforms, AxionPay
daniel.park@axionpay.com

Thanks Daniel — completely understood. Quick answers + what we’re doing next: 

- Latency: Pinning to v4.3.2 will not change your serving tier or instance type; the runtime will route to the pinned model variant. We’ve validated on our infra that P50/P95 are within 5% of current numbers for comparable requests on standard 16-token batches. I’ve attached a micro-benchmark snapshot (axion_benchmarks_summary.xlsx) with P50/P95 numbers.
- Diff examples: see attached diffs_summary (diffs_v4.4_vs_v4.3.2_summary.txt) — highlights include tokenization boundary shifts on hyphenated entity labels and one prompt family where completion suffixing changed. I also pushed a small sample golden-set to the eval console: https://redwood.example.com/evals/AXP-1147/results (view-only link in related links).

Next steps I’ll take now:
1) Prepare the snapshot and lock routing to v4.3.2 for AxionPay in a maintenance-safe mode. This is reversible.
2) Share a short verification checklist your engineering/security team can run (I’m attaching eval_prompts_axion.txt).
3) Coordinate with Rishi & Priyom internally to run a targeted diff triage; we’ll produce an executive summary and recommended remediation within 48 hours.

If AxionPay confirms the temporary hold, we’ll schedule the pin for a 30-minute low-traffic window and notify your team before the change. Please confirm preferred time window (est morning or late evening PST).

Attachments: diffs_v4.4_vs_v4.3.2_summary.txt; eval_prompts_axion.txt; axion_benchmarks_summary.xlsx

Thanks —
Marissa

- Legal / Sales: Marissa, please flag whether we need an SLA credit hold before executing the pin (if they request backdated credits we’ll need approvals).

Daniel — we can hold routing to v4.3.2 now upon your written confirmation. If you prefer a maintenance window, suggest Tue 11/3 23:00 PST and we’ll execute and confirm the change. Post-pin, we’ll provide: the diff summary, a remediation plan (if needed), and a rollback checklist.
